name: Masala Omelette
instructions: Finely chop the onion, tomato (seeds removed) and green chilli, and roughly chop the coriander.
Crack the 4 eggs into a bowl, add the turmeric and a pinch of salt and pepper, and whisk until frothy.
Stir the onion, tomato, chilli and half the coriander into the eggs.
Heat half the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat until it shimmers.
Pour in half the egg mixture and tilt the pan so it covers the base evenly.
Cook for 2–3 minutes until the edges set and the underside is golden, lifting the edges with a spatula.
Fold the omelette in half and cook 1 more minute; slide it onto a plate and repeat with the rest.
Toast the bread, sprinkle the omelettes with the remaining coriander and serve straight away.

name: Kanda Poha
instructions: Put the flattened rice in a sieve and rinse under cold water for 20–30 seconds until just soft; drain and leave for 5 minutes.
Finely chop the onion and green chilli; chop the coriander.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the peanuts for 2 minutes until golden; lift them out.
Add the onion and chilli to the pan and cook for 3–4 minutes until the onion is soft and translucent.
Stir in the turmeric and the peas and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the rinsed rice and a pinch of salt and sugar, and fold gently for 2 minutes until evenly yellow and hot.
Turn off the heat, squeeze over the lemon juice and mix in the peanuts.
Scatter with coriander and serve warm.

name: Red Lentil Dal
instructions: Rinse the lentils in a sieve until the water runs clear.
Put the lentils in a pan with 600 ml water and the turmeric; bring to the boil, skim off the foam and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
Meanwhile rinse the rice and cook it in 300 ml salted water, covered, on the lowest heat for 12 minutes; leave covered off the heat for 5 minutes.
Finely chop the onion, grate the garlic and ginger, and chop the tomatoes.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat, add the cumin and let it sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and fry for 6–8 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and garam masala and cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Stir the onion mixture into the lentils, season with salt and simmer for 3 more minutes; add a splash of water if it's too thick.
Serve the dal over the rice, sprinkled with coriander.

name: Chana Masala
instructions: Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Finely chop the onion and grate the garlic and ginger.
Rinse the rice and cook it in 300 ml salted water, covered, on the lowest heat for 12 minutes; rest it off the heat for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat; add the cumin and fry for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until deep golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric and garam masala and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until thickened.
Add the chickpeas and 100 ml water, season with salt and simmer for 10 minutes; mash a few chickpeas against the side to thicken the sauce.
Scatter with coriander and serve with the rice.

name: Palak Paneer
instructions: Bring a pan of water to the boil, add the spinach for 1 minute, then drain and cool it under cold water.
Blend the spinach with the green chilli and 3 tablespoons of water to a smooth purée.
Cut the paneer into 2 cm cubes; chop the onion and tomatoes; grate the garlic and ginger.
Cook the rice in 300 ml salted water, covered, on the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then rest 5 minutes.
Heat half the oil in a frying pan and fry the paneer for 4–5 minutes, turning, until golden; set aside.
Add the rest of the oil and the cumin, then the onion; cook for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes until jammy.
Stir in the spinach purée and garam masala, season with salt and simmer for 3 minutes.
Take off the heat, stir in the yogurt, then fold in the paneer. Serve with the rice.

name: Chicken Tikka Masala
instructions: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and mix with the yogurt, half the garam masala, the turmeric, paprika and a pinch of salt; leave for at least 10 minutes.
Rinse the rice and cook it in 300 ml salted water, covered, on the lowest heat for 12 minutes; rest it for 5 minutes.
Heat half the oil in a large frying pan over high heat and brown the chicken for 5–6 minutes; set aside (it will finish cooking in the sauce).
Lower the heat to medium, add the rest of the oil and the finely chopped onion, and cook for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the grated garlic and ginger and the rest of the garam masala; stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 8 minutes until thick.
Stir in the cream, return the chicken and simmer for 6–8 minutes until it is cooked through (no pink in the middle).
Season to taste and serve with the rice.

name: Aloo Gobi
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes; cut the cauliflower into small florets.
Rinse the rice and cook it in 240 ml salted water, covered, on the lowest heat for 12 minutes; rest it for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large lidded pan over medium heat; add the cumin and fry for 30 seconds.
Add the chopped onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft, then the grated garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, turmeric and a teaspoon of salt and stir to coat; cook for 5 minutes.
Add the cauliflower and chopped tomatoes with 3 tablespoons of water, cover and cook on low heat for 15 minutes, stirring gently twice, until the potatoes are tender.
Uncover, sprinkle with garam masala and cook for 2 more minutes to dry slightly.
Scatter with coriander and serve with the rice.

name: Vegetable Frittata
instructions: Heat the oven grill to high. Slice the courgette and onion thinly and halve the tomatoes.
Whisk the 5 eggs with the grated parmesan and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in an oven-safe frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion and courgette for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the spinach and stir for 1 minute until wilted; spread the vegetables evenly.
Pour in the eggs, scatter the tomatoes on top and cook without stirring for 6–8 minutes until the edges are set.
Put the pan under the grill for 3–4 minutes until the top is puffed and golden.
Leave for 2 minutes, loosen the edges and slide onto a board; cut into wedges.

name: Bruschetta al Pomodoro
instructions: Cut the tomatoes into small dice and put them in a sieve over a bowl for 5 minutes to drain.
Mix the tomatoes with the torn basil, 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, the vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Cut the bread into 4 thick slices.
Toast or grill the bread for 2 minutes a side until crisp and charred at the edges.
Rub one side of each hot slice with the halved garlic clove.
Drizzle with the rest of the oil and pile the tomatoes on top just before eating.

name: Tomato Basil Pasta
instructions: Bring a large pan of well-salted water to the boil.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and thinly slice the garlic.
Cook the pasta for the time on the pack minus 1 minute; keep a mug of the cooking water before draining.
Meanwhile heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and fry the garlic and chilli for 1 minute without browning.
Add the tomatoes with a pinch of salt and cook for 6–8 minutes, pressing some with a spoon, until saucy.
Add the drained pasta and a splash of the cooking water and toss for 1 minute so the sauce clings.
Tear in the basil, season with pepper and serve.

name: Mushroom Risotto
instructions: Heat the stock in a pan and keep it at a gentle simmer.
Slice the mushrooms; finely chop the onion, garlic and parsley.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat and fry the mushrooms for 5 minutes until golden; season and set aside.
Lower the heat to medium, add half the butter and the onion and cook for 4 minutes until soft; add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the rice and stir for 1–2 minutes until the edges look translucent.
Add a ladle of hot stock and stir until it is absorbed; keep adding stock a ladle at a time, stirring often, for 18–20 minutes until the rice is creamy and just tender.
Stir in the mushrooms, the rest of the butter and the grated parmesan; take off the heat and leave covered for 2 minutes.
Season to taste and serve sprinkled with parsley.

name: Spaghetti Bolognese
instructions: Finely chop the onion and carrot and crush the garlic.
Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes until soft.
Turn the heat up, add the mince and cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned all over.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes, oregano and 100 ml water, season, and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
With 10 minutes to go, cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente; drain.
Toss the spaghetti with a little of the sauce, then serve with the rest of the sauce on top and the grated parmesan.

name: Minestrone
instructions: Dice the onion, carrots and courgette into 1 cm pieces; cut the green beans into 2 cm lengths; crush the garlic.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion and carrots for 8 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and courgette and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes and stock, bring to the boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the pasta, green beans and the drained beans and simmer for 10 minutes more until the pasta is tender.
Season well with salt and pepper; add a little water if the soup is too thick.
Ladle into bowls and top with torn basil and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Baked Cod with Tomatoes and Olives
instructions: Heat the oven to 200 °C (fan 180 °C).
Cut the potatoes into 2 cm chunks, toss with half the oil and salt in a baking dish and roast for 15 minutes.
Halve the tomatoes, slice the garlic and halve the olives.
Add the tomatoes, olives and garlic to the dish, drizzle with the rest of the oil and stir.
Season the cod, lay it on top of the vegetables and add 2 slices of lemon.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until the fish flakes easily and is opaque all the way through.
Squeeze over the rest of the lemon, scatter with parsley and serve.

name: Apple Cinnamon Porridge
instructions: Core the apple; grate half of it and cut the other half into thin slices.
Put the oats, oat milk, grated apple, raisins and half the cinnamon in a pan with a pinch of salt.
Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, stirring.
Lower the heat and simmer for 5–6 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy; add a splash of water if needed.
Roughly chop the walnuts.
Spoon into bowls and top with the apple slices, walnuts and the rest of the cinnamon.

name: Uitsmijter with Cheese
instructions: Butter the bread lightly with a third of the butter and put two slices on each plate.
Cover the bread with the sliced Gouda.
Melt the rest of the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Crack in the 4 eggs and fry for 3–4 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft (or longer if you like them firm).
Season the eggs with salt and pepper and slide two onto each plate of bread and cheese; the heat melts the cheese.
Serve with the tomato, sliced.

name: Pan-Seared Salmon
instructions: Peel the potatoes, cut them into even pieces and boil in salted water for 18–20 minutes until tender; drain.
Cut the broccoli into florets and steam or boil it for the last 5 minutes of the potatoes' cooking time.
Pat the salmon dry with kitchen paper and season with salt and pepper.
Heat half the butter in a frying pan over medium-high heat and lay the salmon in skin side down.
Cook for 4–5 minutes without moving it until the skin is crisp, then turn and cook 2–3 minutes more until just cooked through.
Toss the potatoes with the rest of the butter and the chopped dill.
Serve the salmon with the potatoes, broccoli and lemon wedges.

name: Boerenkool Stamppot with Smoked Sausage
instructions: Peel the potatoes, cut them into chunks and put them in a large pan with salted water.
Put the chopped kale on top of the potatoes, bring to the boil, cover and cook for 20 minutes until the potatoes are soft.
Meanwhile heat the smoked sausage in hot (not boiling) water for 15–20 minutes, or as the pack says.
Warm the milk.
Drain the potatoes and kale and mash them together with the butter and warm milk until smooth but still with texture.
Season with salt and pepper and stir in a little mustard if you like.
Slice the sausage and serve on the stamppot with more mustard on the side.

name: Hutspot with Crispy Chickpeas
instructions: Peel and chop the potatoes and carrots into similar-sized chunks; slice the onions.
Put the potatoes and carrots in a pan, lay the onions on top, add salted water to just cover and boil for 20 minutes until soft.
Meanwhile drain the chickpeas and pat them very dry with kitchen paper.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the chickpeas for 8–10 minutes, shaking the pan, until crisp.
Toss the chickpeas with the smoked paprika and a pinch of salt.
Drain the vegetables, keeping a little of the cooking water, and mash them roughly with the warm oat milk.
Season the hutspot well and serve topped with the crispy chickpeas.

name: Erwtensoep
instructions: Rinse the split peas in a sieve.
Put the peas, stock and bacon in a large pot, bring to the boil and skim off the foam.
Simmer with the lid ajar for 45 minutes, stirring now and then so it doesn't stick.
Meanwhile dice the onion, carrots and potatoes and slice the leek.
Add the vegetables to the pot and simmer for 30–40 minutes more until the peas have fallen apart and the soup is thick.
For the last 15 minutes, add the whole smoked sausage to heat through.
Take out the sausage, slice it and return it to the soup.
Season with salt and pepper; the soup thickens as it stands, so add hot water if it gets too thick.

name: Andijvie Stamppot with Gouda
instructions: Peel and quarter the potatoes and boil them in salted water for 20 minutes until soft.
Wash the endive, dry it well and cut it into thin strips.
Cut the Gouda into small cubes and roughly chop the walnuts.
Warm the milk.
Drain the potatoes and mash them with the butter and warm milk.
Stir the raw endive through the hot mash in batches so it just wilts.
Fold in the cheese, season with salt, pepper and a little nutmeg if you have it, and scatter with walnuts.

name: Bruine Bonensoep
instructions: Chop the onion and carrots, slice the leek and crush the garlic.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, carrots and leek for 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, smoked paprika and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beans with their liquid and the stock; bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes.
Blend about half of the soup with a stick blender so it thickens but keeps some whole beans.
Season with salt and pepper and simmer for 5 more minutes; add water if it's too thick.
Serve with the bread.

name: Mushroom Congee
instructions: Rinse the rice, then put it in a pot with the stock and the ginger cut into thin matchsticks.
Bring to the boil, then simmer on low heat with the lid ajar for 40 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until thick and porridge-like.
Meanwhile slice the mushrooms and garlic and quarter the pak choi.
Heat a little sesame oil in a frying pan and fry the mushrooms for 5 minutes until golden; add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the pak choi to the congee for the last 3 minutes.
Season the congee with the soy sauce and add hot water if it's too thick.
Serve topped with the mushrooms, sliced spring onions and a drizzle of sesame oil.

name: Tamagoyaki Rice Bowl
instructions: Rinse the rice and cook it in 210 ml water, covered, on the lowest heat for 12 minutes; rest it for 5 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the soy sauce, sugar and a pinch of salt.
Heat a little oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat and pour in a thin layer of egg.
When it's almost set, roll it up from one side to the other with chopsticks or a spatula.
Push the roll back to the start, oil the pan again and pour in another thin layer, lifting the roll so egg runs underneath; roll up again.
Repeat until all the egg is used, then cut the omelette into thick slices.
Slice the cucumber thinly and the spring onions finely.
Serve the egg on the rice with the cucumber, spring onions and sesame seeds.

name: Chicken Rice Bowl
instructions: Rinse the rice and cook it in 225 ml water, covered, on the lowest heat for 12 minutes; rest it for 5 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, honey, grated garlic and ginger with 2 tablespoons of water to make the sauce.
Cut the chicken into strips, the broccoli into small florets and the carrot into thin matchsticks.
Heat the sesame oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat and stir-fry the chicken for 5–6 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Add the broccoli, carrot and 2 tablespoons of water and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until just tender.
Pour in the sauce and toss for 1 minute until everything is glossy.
Spoon over the rice and top with sliced spring onions and sesame seeds.

name: Thai Vegetable Stir-Fry
instructions: Rinse the rice and cook it in 225 ml water, covered, on the lowest heat for 12 minutes; rest it for 5 minutes.
Slice the pepper, cut the broccoli into small florets, cut the carrot into matchsticks and quarter the pak choi.
Mix the soy sauce with the juice of the lime and 2 tablespoons of water.
Roughly chop the peanuts and toast them in a dry wok for 2 minutes; set aside.
Heat the oil in the wok over high heat and stir-fry the grated garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the carrot and broccoli and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then the pepper for 2 minutes.
Add the pak choi and the sauce and toss for 1–2 minutes until the leaves wilt.
Serve over the rice, topped with the peanuts and sliced spring onions.

name: Thai Red Chicken Curry
instructions: Rinse the rice and cook it in 225 ml water, covered, on the lowest heat for 12 minutes; rest it for 5 minutes.
Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces, slice the pepper and halve the green beans.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep pan over medium heat and fry the curry paste for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir for 3 minutes to coat it in the paste.
Pour in the coconut milk, bring to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the green beans and pepper and simmer for 5 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Season with the fish sauce and the juice of half the lime.
Stir in the basil leaves and serve with the rice and lime wedges.

name: Teriyaki Tofu
instructions: Drain the tofu, wrap it in a clean tea towel and press it under something heavy for 10 minutes; cut it into 2 cm cubes.
Rinse the rice and cook it in 225 ml water, covered, on the lowest heat for 12 minutes; rest it for 5 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, grated ginger and garlic with 3 tablespoons of water.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 8–10 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides.
Steam or boil the broccoli florets for 4 minutes until bright green.
Pour the sauce over the tofu and let it bubble for 2–3 minutes, tossing, until thick and glossy.
Serve the tofu and broccoli over the rice with sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.

name: Garlic Prawn Noodles
instructions: Cook the noodles as the pack says, drain and rinse them under cold water so they don't stick.
Thinly slice the garlic, chilli and spring onions; grate the ginger; quarter the pak choi.
Heat the sesame oil in a wok over high heat and fry the garlic, ginger and chilli for 30 seconds.
Add the prawns and stir-fry for 2–3 minutes until pink all over.
Add the pak choi and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the noodles and soy sauce and toss for 2 minutes until hot.
Squeeze over the lime and serve topped with the spring onions.

name: Huevos Rancheros
instructions: Finely chop the onion, garlic and chilli.
Heat half the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes, then the garlic and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and the drained beans, season and simmer for 8 minutes until thick.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side and keep them wrapped in a tea towel.
Make 4 hollows in the sauce, crack an egg into each, cover and cook for 5–6 minutes until the whites are set.
Slice the avocado.
Put two tortillas on each plate, spoon over the sauce and eggs, and top with avocado and coriander.

name: Breakfast Burrito
instructions: Make a quick salsa: dice the tomato, chop the coriander and mix with a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt.
Dice the pepper and drain the beans.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the pepper for 3 minutes; add the beans and warm through for 2 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper, pour them into the pan and stir gently for 2–3 minutes until softly scrambled.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds a side.
Divide the egg mixture between the tortillas, top with grated cheddar and salsa.
Fold in the sides, roll up tightly and cut in half to serve.

name: Black Bean Tacos
instructions: Drain and rinse the beans and the sweetcorn.
Finely chop the red onion and the tomatoes; mix half the onion with the tomatoes, a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt for a salsa.
Mash the avocado with the juice of half the lime and a pinch of salt.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the rest of the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the beans, sweetcorn, cumin, paprika and 3 tablespoons of water; cook for 5 minutes, crushing some beans with a fork.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side.
Fill the tortillas with the beans, avocado and salsa, and top with coriander and lime wedges.

name: Chicken Fajitas
instructions: Cut the chicken into thin strips and the peppers and onion into slices.
Mix the chicken with the paprika, cumin, crushed garlic, half the oil, the juice of half the lime and a pinch of salt.
Heat a large frying pan over high heat until very hot.
Cook the chicken for 5–6 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through; set aside.
Add the rest of the oil and stir-fry the peppers and onion for 5 minutes until softened and charred at the edges.
Return the chicken, toss together and squeeze over the rest of the lime.
Warm the tortillas and serve with the filling, sliced avocado and the yogurt.

name: Chili sin Carne
instructions: Chop the onion and pepper and crush the garlic; drain and rinse the beans and sweetcorn.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion and pepper for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and chilli flakes and stir for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the chopped tomatoes and 150 ml water.
Add the beans, season and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Meanwhile rinse the rice and cook it in 375 ml water, covered, on the lowest heat for 12 minutes; rest it for 5 minutes.
Stir the sweetcorn into the chili for the last 5 minutes.
Taste and adjust the salt and heat, then serve with the rice.

name: Chili con Carne
instructions: Chop the onion and pepper, crush the garlic and drain the beans.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the mince for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up.
Add the onion and pepper and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and 150 ml water, season, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the beans and simmer for 10 minutes more until thick.
Meanwhile rinse the rice and cook it in 375 ml water, covered, on the lowest heat for 12 minutes; rest it for 5 minutes.
Serve the chili over the rice.

name: Fish Tacos
instructions: Finely shred the red cabbage and toss it with the juice of half the lime and a pinch of salt.
Mix the yogurt with a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt for the sauce.
Pat the cod dry, cut it into 4 pieces and rub with the paprika, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the cod for 3 minutes a side until it flakes easily.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side.
Slice the avocado.
Flake the fish into the tortillas and top with the cabbage, avocado, yogurt sauce and coriander.

name: Greek Yogurt with Honey and Walnuts
instructions: Thaw the berries if frozen (a few minutes at room temperature or 30 seconds in the microwave).
Roughly chop the walnuts and toast them in a dry pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until fragrant.
Divide the yogurt between two bowls.
Top with the berries and granola.
Scatter over the walnuts.
Drizzle with the honey and serve straight away so the granola stays crunchy.

name: Strapatsada
instructions: Grate the tomatoes on the coarse side of a grater, discarding the skins; finely chop the onion.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the grated tomato and a pinch of salt and simmer for 6–8 minutes until most of the liquid has gone.
Lightly beat the eggs and pour them into the pan.
Stir gently for 2–3 minutes until just set and creamy.
Crumble over the feta and sprinkle with oregano and pepper.
Serve with the bread, toasted, for dipping.

name: Greek Village Salad
instructions: Cut the tomatoes into wedges and the cucumber into thick half-moons.
Slice the red onion and the green pepper into thin rings.
Put the vegetables and olives in a bowl, season with a little salt and toss gently.
Whisk the olive oil with the vinegar.
Lay the feta on top of the salad in one slab and sprinkle with oregano.
Drizzle over the dressing.
Warm the pita in a dry pan or toaster and serve alongside to mop up the juices.

name: Chicken Souvlaki with Tzatziki
instructions: Cut the chicken into 3 cm cubes and mix with the juice of half the lemon, half the crushed garlic, the oregano, 2 tablespoons of oil and salt; leave for 15 minutes.
Grate the cucumber, squeeze out the water with your hands and mix with the yogurt, the rest of the garlic, the chopped dill and a pinch of salt.
Thread the chicken onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water first).
Heat a griddle pan or frying pan over high heat and cook the skewers for 10–12 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Slice the tomatoes and red onion.
Warm the pitas.
Serve the chicken on the pitas with the tomatoes, onion, tzatziki and lemon wedges.

name: Gigantes Plaki
instructions: Heat the oven to 190 °C (fan 170 °C).
Finely chop the onion and carrots and crush the garlic; drain and rinse the beans.
Heat the oil in an oven-safe pan over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and oregano for 1 minute, then the chopped tomatoes and 150 ml water; season and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the beans and half the chopped herbs.
Bake uncovered for 30 minutes until the sauce is thick and the top slightly crisp.
Scatter with the rest of the herbs and serve warm with the bread.

name: Garides Saganaki
instructions: Finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the oil in an oven-safe frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes; add the garlic and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, season and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Heat the oven grill to high.
Stir the prawns into the sauce and cook for 3 minutes until just pink.
Crumble the feta over the top and grill for 3–4 minutes until it softens and browns at the edges.
Scatter with parsley and serve with the bread.

name: Briam
instructions: Heat the oven to 200 °C (fan 180 °C).
Cut the potatoes into thin slices and the courgette, aubergine and onion into 1 cm slices.
Grate 1 tomato and slice the rest; crush the garlic.
Toss all the vegetables with the grated tomato, garlic, oregano, olive oil, salt and pepper in a baking dish.
Add 100 ml water, cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes.
Uncover, stir gently and bake for 20 more minutes until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden.
Scatter with parsley and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Herb Omelette
instructions: Finely chop the herbs and grate the Gruyère.
Beat 5 eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper until just combined; stir in most of the herbs.
Melt half the butter in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat until it foams.
Pour in half the eggs and stir quickly with a spatula for 20 seconds, then let them settle into an even layer.
When the top is still slightly runny, sprinkle half the cheese over one side.
Fold the omelette in thirds and roll it onto a plate; make the second one the same way.
Scatter with the rest of the herbs and serve with the baguette.

name: Pain Perdu
instructions: Cut the baguette into 2 cm slices (day-old bread works best).
Whisk the eggs, milk and cinnamon in a shallow dish.
Soak the bread in the mixture for 30 seconds a side.
Melt half the butter in a frying pan over medium heat.
Fry half the bread for 2–3 minutes a side until golden; repeat with the rest of the butter and bread.
Warm the berries in a small pan for 2 minutes until juicy.
Serve the toast topped with the berries and a drizzle of honey.

name: Ratatouille
instructions: Cut the aubergine, courgettes and peppers into 2 cm pieces; chop the onion and tomatoes; crush the garlic.
Heat half the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and fry the aubergine for 6–8 minutes until golden; set aside.
Fry the courgettes for 5 minutes in a little more oil; set aside.
Add the rest of the oil and cook the onion and peppers for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and oregano for 1 minute, then the tomatoes; simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the aubergine and courgettes, season and simmer gently, covered, for 15 minutes.
Stir in the torn basil and serve warm with the baguette.

name: Chicken Chasseur
instructions: Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 5 minutes a side; set aside.
Lower the heat, add the chopped onion and sliced mushrooms and cook for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and stock, return the chicken, cover and simmer for 25 minutes until cooked through.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes in salted water for 18–20 minutes until tender.
Uncover the chicken for the last 5 minutes so the sauce thickens.
Scatter with parsley and serve with the potatoes.

name: Salade Niçoise
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until tender; add the green beans for the last 4 minutes; drain and cool under cold water.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool them in cold water, then peel and quarter them.
Halve the potatoes and tomatoes and thinly slice the red onion.
Whisk the olive oil, mustard and vinegar with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Toss the potatoes, beans, tomatoes and onion with half the dressing.
Arrange on plates and top with the drained tuna, eggs and olives.
Drizzle over the rest of the dressing.

name: French Onion Soup
instructions: Thinly slice the onions.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium-low heat, add the onions and a pinch of salt and cook for 35–40 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until deep golden and sticky; add the sugar halfway.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock gradually, stirring, then simmer for 10 minutes; season with salt and pepper.
Heat the oven grill to high and toast slices of baguette on both sides.
Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls, float the toast on top and cover with the grated Gruyère.
Grill for 2–3 minutes until the cheese bubbles and browns.

name: Lentil Salad with Mustard Dressing
instructions: Rinse the lentils and put them in a pan with the peeled garlic clove and plenty of cold water.
Bring to the boil and simmer for 20–25 minutes until tender but still holding their shape; drain and remove the garlic.
Meanwhile dice the carrot finely and the red onion very finely; halve the tomatoes.
Whisk the mustard, vinegar and olive oil with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Toss the warm lentils with the dressing so they soak it up.
Fold in the carrot, onion, tomatoes and chopped parsley.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
